predecessors.name: Kingdom of Serbia (Nemanjić state)
predecessors.text: northern Serbia along the Hungarian border including the Rudnik silver mine, kept by Dragutin when he abdicated at Deževo in 1282

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Hungary
predecessors.text: Mačva, granted with Usora and Soli by Ladislaus IV of Hungary in the second half of 1284

successors.name: Kingdom of Serbia (Nemanjić state)
successors.text: Dečanski's Serbia, which took Vladislav II's northern domains after the victory of 1324

successors.name: Kingdom of Hungary
successors.text: 'Lower Syrmia', disputed between Serbia and Hungary after 1324

successors.name: Banate of Bosnia
successors.text: Usora and Soli (Soli read as the Tuzla salt district, Usora as Doboj: the researcher's reading)

ledger.x: Second half of 1284: Hungary grants Mačva, Usora and Soli.

ledger.cp: Darman and Kudelin (Bulgarian boyars of Cuman origin, lords of Braničevo and Kučevo)

ledger.x: 1301: war with Milutin; Rudnik is lost.

c. 1312: peace with Milutin and Rudnik returns. Milutin 'defeated Dragutin in late 1311 or 1312, and a peace was probably mediated in 1312'; Dragutin 'recognized Milutin as lawful king and got his Serbian territories, including Rudnik, back'. The shape is whole again from 1312 (kingdom-of-syrmia_1294, valid from 1312).
1325: Usora and Soli pass to Bosnia.

wars.name: Dragutin's invasion of Braničevo
wars.outcome: Failed in 1284 or 1285; Dragutin and Milutin defeated Darman and Kudelin and took Braničevo in 1292 (Darman and Kudelin page; the Dragutin page: '1291 or 1292').

wars.name: War between Dragutin and Milutin
wars.outcome: Milutin took Rudnik in 1301; a peace of late 1302 failed; Milutin defeated Dragutin in late 1311 or 1312 and a peace of about 1312 gave Dragutin back his Serbian lands including Rudnik, Dragutin recognising Milutin as king.

wars.name: Dečanski's war against Stefan Vladislav II
wars.outcome: Dečanski defeated Vladislav II in 1324; Vladislav's rule ended in 1325 and 'Lower Syrmia' became disputed between Serbia and Hungary.

certainty.note: The pages name rivers and mines (the Sava, Rudnik, the Lim) but no boundary; Usora and Soli were Hungarian banates held as fiefs.
